checklist.bullet: GIPPA runs end to end on A1, A2 and A3
A1 and A2 detections and abundances are compared

checklist.evidence: metrics.json › te_real.te2-te5.status; TE4 not passed: report_notes.md › Diagnosis: TE4

caveats: The score bins span the de novo scores of (0.8, 1] only (Cascadia's reported range).
c_value comes from A2's own exact matches and the confirmations from A2's identifications, so A2 enters both sides: a shared dependence, not an independent check.
Class error rates of A3's ALT calls are unestimated (no spectrum pairing).

Dependent rows: nested or overlapping de novo peptides of one locus share correctness, so the genome bin CI can be too narrow and a not_supported can come from that undercoverage; nested_share shows how clustered each bin is.

Contaminant rows count in c_value (they never match the genome), which biases the genome precision up and lowers the power to refute; de novo contaminant peptides are not in A2's set and count as unconfirmed.
A2's identifications are at 1 % FDR, so the lower bound can be off by up to that share (not corrected).
A failure confined to a single score bin reads consistent_with_lower_bound: not_supported needs two consecutive reportable bins below the bound (the pre-registered fallback).
h4.searchable_definition: GIPPA's digest (trypsin_p, at most 1 missed cleavage, 7-30 residues, no N-terminal Met excision; not DIA-NN's settings) of --strain-db, I folded to L

caveats: near-homolog entrapment: the estimate errs high (§15.5)
